page: OVHcloud c3-4 is a compute-optimized instance hosted on KVM hypervisors, powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration provides two dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, resulting in two dedicated vCPUs. Memory allocation is set at 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per core, with 32 MB of Level 3 cache. Bundled local storage includes a 50 GB NVMe SSD. No dedicated GPUs are included, and the baseline network bandwidth is designated at 0 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-core throughput alongside expected multi-core scaling limits. The instance records a strong stress-ng single-core result of 3083.56, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems, while its multi-core stress-ng performance reaches 6125.55. Geekbench evaluates single-core performance at 1910.0 and multi-core at 3412.0. Memory bandwidth remains steady at 61.56 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 29.93 GB/sec for writes. PassMark metrics reflect entry-tier parallel throughput with a CPU score of 5442.44, whereas lightweight LLM text generation achieves 145.21 tokens per second on a small 135M model.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a resource-dense configuration for compute tasks that do not demand extensive memory allocations. The combination of dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores and integrated NVMe storage offers consistent execution times without the variance common to shared-core models. However, the limited total memory footprint and low baseline network profile constrain scalability for network-heavy distribution and expansive memory buffers.

OVHcloud c3-4 is well suited for targeted microservices, lightweight continuous integration workers, entry-level batch compute processes, and small web backend jobs where dedicated execution and fast local disk access are preferred over high memory capacity.

It features two dedicated physical cores mapped directly to two vCPUs without hyperthreading, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, 32 MB of L3 cache, and a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD. The instance contains zero GPUs and specifies a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance delivers strong single-core CPU throughput via stress-ng, accompanied by moderate large-block memory bandwidth. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides cost-efficient CPU resource allocation for tasks requiring consistent, non-shared compute capacity rather than expansive memory. The server is well suited for microservices, lightweight compilation, batch automation scripts, and modest backend web serving.
